title: Choose offsite backup storage provider
description: Decide where the offsite copy of the restic repositories lives before implementing the copy itself. Compare Backblaze B2, S3-compatible object storage and a second physical site/NAS on cost, egress, restic/rclone support, credential handling via sops, encryption, and how the restore drill reaches it. Record the decision and its rationale in this bead; the implementation is nix-workloads-o1m.
acceptance_criteria: A provider/site is chosen and recorded with rationale, rough monthly cost, egress/restore implications, and the sops/age credential path. The choice must survive loss of both Pis; a two-node Garage backend is not offsite. This clears the 4ge blocker on nix-workloads-o1m, which also waits for nix-workloads-dso.
notes: Related design input: a Garage/S3 backend on both hosts (nix-workloads-6zs) can remove the single-host-loss asymmetry and be the source for the copy, but two nodes are not offsite. The chosen provider must still survive loss of both Pis; do not let the Garage option turn o1m into a no-op.

title: Copy restic backups offsite
description:
Known risk: losing both Pi hosts loses the backup data. Restic repositories live on rpi5-4gb; Attic (a regenerable build cache) lives on the default host rpi5-8gb and is not a backup. Scope this bead to the restic repositories only.

Decide and implement the durable path, with nix-workloads-4ge choosing the provider:
- offsite copy of each restic repo (B2/S3/second site, restic/rclone), or
- a replicated S3 backend such as Garage (nix-workloads-6zs) used directly by restic, with a restic endpoint/service on each host. Evaluate resource cost (memory/CPU/disk) against the 4GB host before committing; note that a two-node Garage layout has quorum/replication trade-offs and must still be verified against loss of either host.

Sequence: nix-workloads-dso must land first so per-guest credentials exist; copying a shared-credential repo offsite would spread the blast radius. Include the copy in the restore drill and close only after a restore from the offsite/replicated copy succeeds.

Cross-link: 4ge (provider), dso (auth), 6zs (Garage option), 5th/3kb (drill), 1hg (state backend, if Garage is chosen).
acceptance_criteria: Every restic repository has a copy that survives loss of both Pis, off the pair: an offsite provider chosen in nix-workloads-4ge, or a documented second site. A replicated Garage/per-host restic path (nix-workloads-6zs) can remove the single-host-loss asymmetry and can be the source of the offsite copy, but two nodes are not offsite and do not by themselves satisfy this bead. A restore of at least one guest's snapshot from the copy succeeds and is added to the restore drill (nix-workloads-5th / nix-workloads-3kb). nix-workloads-dso lands first: no shared-credential repo is copied offsite. Credentials come from sops with a documented recovery path. Incremental memory/CPU/disk cost is measured and recorded. Attic is explicitly out of scope as a regenerable cache.
notes: Extend the basic restore drill (nix-workloads-5th) to include the offsite copy once it exists; close only after a restore from the offsite repository succeeds.

title: Total-site-loss recovery in under an hour
description:
North-star goal: the whole lab can be rebuilt from git and off-pair storage onto fresh hardware within an hour, not just onto the surviving Pi.

Scope: both Pi hosts (host OS from nix-homelab-hosts, DNS zone, step-ca, Kanidm, Attic/restic, monitoring), the physical Zigbee coordinator move, and data restore. The external build cache (Cachix) is deliberately not on the critical path; a restore that works without it is allowed.

Current tranches: nix-workloads-o1m (off-pair copy), nix-workloads-sl8 (MTTR onto the survivor), nix-workloads-m2x (provision from empty), nix-workloads-5th and nix-workloads-3kb (drills), nix-workloads-dh7 (coverage), nix-workloads-c6z (RTO/RPO model).

Success is a timed, repeated drill with published numbers, not a runbook nobody runs.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, timed total-site-loss drill restores all critical services onto fresh hardware, including host OS, DNS, certs, identity, MQTT/Zigbee and data, from off-pair storage. Published RTO/RPO targets (target: RTO <= 60 min, RPO <= 24h) are met and measured. Lights, heating and MQTT are verified after restore. The drill is repeated at least quarterly with results recorded. Gaps are filed and fixed.

title: Add Kanidm break-glass and identity-outage runbook
description: Kanidm is the OIDC root for the admin UIs, and its data is backed up and restored by the drill, but there is no break-glass path or runbook for Kanidm being down, locked out, or needing admin recovery. `ka7` lists DNS, certificate, disk and monitoring failures but not identity. Add a local break-glass admin path that does not depend on Kanidm for oauth2-proxy-protected endpoints, document Kanidm down, lockout, admin-credential loss and restore, and test access after a restore. Record which UIs are intentionally unavailable without identity.
acceptance_criteria: A break-glass admin path is documented and tested without Kanidm. A Kanidm outage, lockout and admin-recovery playbook is checked in with symptoms, checks, mitigation and verification. Each OIDC-protected UI has an explicit fallback or accepted lockout. Kanidm restore plus access is verified with dr-restore. ka7, 485, 182, rp6 and 8xp are cross-linked.

title: Own the CA hierarchy: root key custody, expiry and rotation
description: The dkp epic covers leaf certificates, and `certs/` contains only the public root and intermediate certificates. Nothing tracks custody, offline backup, expiry or rotation of the root CA private key, the intermediate private key beyond sops, or the fact that dev reuses the production intermediate and can mint production-trusted certificates. Define where the root key lives offline, how it is backed up and restored, how root and intermediate expiry is monitored, how the intermediate is rotated and leaves reissued, and what happens on root compromise. Decide whether dev keeps the production intermediate or gets its own intermediate under the same root, with compensating controls if the trade-off is accepted.
acceptance_criteria: Root and intermediate key custody is documented, including the offline location and who can access it. An offline backup or escrow exists and has been tested. Expiry alerting covers the root and intermediate, not just leaves. An intermediate rotation and leaf reissue runbook is checked in and rehearsed at least in dev. The dev CA trade-off is decided (separate intermediate or accepted with compensating controls). Linked to dkp, dkp.2, 182, 8xp and rp6.

title: Enforce backup and snapshot coverage for stateful workloads
description:
Backup is opt-in: `local.backup.paths` defaults to empty, so a new stateful guest is silently unprotected. Custom volumes get snapshot policies per workload, but no check asserts that a volume-owning guest has a policy, and no bead explicitly rehearses `task restore-snap`.

Add inventory-derived invariants. The check needs an explicit source of truth: add a `stateful` (and optionally `backup = true`) declaration per service in inventory.nix, since the current inventory has no way to tell a stateful guest from a stateless one. Then every declared stateful guest must have backup paths or a recorded exception, and every attached custom volume must have a snapshot policy or a recorded exception.

Exception decided here: `attic-data` has no snapshot policy and no restic backup on purpose. It is a regenerable build cache and AGENTS.md says not to snapshot it; do not "fix" it. Record it in the coverage matrix as an accepted exception. Likewise, do not claim volume snapshots are a backup: they are host-local and crash-consistent.

Add a snapshot-restore drill to the dev restore flow, include mosquitto once nix-workloads-4eg adds persistence, and document the full coverage matrix plus exceptions with reasons in README.
acceptance_criteria: A check fails when a guest declared stateful in inventory.nix has no backup paths and no recorded exception, and when an attached custom volume has no snapshot policy and no recorded exception. attic-data is the documented exception (regenerable cache, not a backup). A snapshot restore is rehearsed in dev and documented. restore-test covers every backed-up guest, including mosquitto after nix-workloads-4eg adds persistence. README contains the coverage matrix and exceptions with reasons. nix-workloads-5th, nix-workloads-3kb and nix-workloads-4eg are cross-linked.

title: Isolate and protect restic repositories (per-guest auth, append-only)
description: `modules/backup.nix` shares one restic REST credential from `secrets/backup.yaml` with every backed-up guest, and `guests/backup/default.nix` runs one htpasswd user. Any guest can list, delete or corrupt every other guest repository. rest-server supports `--private-repos` (the authenticated username must match the first repo path segment) and `--append-only` (clients cannot delete or modify existing snapshots). Implement per-guest users and credentials (user = hostname, repo `/<hostname>`), append-only for guests, and a separate privileged path for retention/prune (run on the backup server or with an admin-only credential). Add a negative test proving guest A cannot read or delete guest B repos, and keep restore-test and dashboards working. dkp.5 adds TLS but does not solve authorization; o1m must not copy a shared-credential repo offsite.
design: Architecture decision to record before implementing: rest-server's --append-only is a server-wide flag, not per-user, so 'append-only for guests plus a privileged prune path' cannot be done with one instance. Choose and document one of: (a) two rest-server instances/ports on different user sets, (b) a front proxy that routes admin/prune vs guest traffic, or (c) a different backend (for example restic to S3/Garage in nix-workloads-6zs) where write-once policy is enforced by bucket credentials. Also verify whether rest-server can require and verify client certificates; if not, mTLS must terminate at nginx/step-ca (nix-workloads-dkp.5).
acceptance_criteria: Every guest has its own credential and can access only its own repository/bucket, using the backend actually chosen (per-guest rest-server users with --private-repos, or per-guest S3 credentials if nix-workloads-6zs replaces rest-server). Guest-side credentials cannot delete or modify snapshots, using a mechanism that is actually supported by the chosen architecture (rest-server's --append-only is global, so per-user append-only needs two instances/ports or an auth-splitting proxy; S3 policy can enforce it per bucket). Retention still runs through a controlled privileged path with tested rollback. A test proves one guest cannot read or delete another guest repo. restore-test and backup dashboards still pass. dkp.5, o1m, 6zs and README are cross-linked and the credential model plus the chosen architecture are documented.

title: Model outage risks, dependencies and second-order effects
description: There is no single model of what can take the smart home down and how failures cascade. Build a checked-in outage model covering host loss, storage or NVMe failure, power loss, router/ISP outage, DNS, CA, Kanidm identity, backup target, build cache, monitoring, the Mac control plane and software regressions. For each scenario record likelihood and impact, affected services, detection, current mitigation, residual risk, owner, and second-order effects (for example DNS loss breaks TLS/MQTT/backups; identity loss locks out admin UIs; cache loss freezes deploys; monitoring loss hides everything). Record explicitly accepted risks (power and router are not being mitigated now) and derive RTO/RPO targets so sl8, env and m2x can be judged. Feed the incident playbooks in ka7 and the maintenance work in xp2.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in model maps every critical service to its dependencies and failure modes. Second-order effects and detection gaps are explicit. Each risk has an owner and a decision (mitigate, accept, transfer) plus residual risk. RTO/RPO targets are recorded. Power and router accepted risks are explicit with rationale. README links the model, and sl8, env, xp2, ka7, 122 and 13n reference it.

title: Rehearse moving a stateful workload between incus hosts
description: `inventory.nix` promises that moving a workload is only a `placement` change, but custom volumes are host-local and are not carried by an instance recreate. No bead exercises a move. Add a runbook and timed rehearsal for moving a stateful guest (for example kanidm or backup) between rpi5-8gb and rpi5-4gb: move data via snapshot/restore or restic, change placement, update DNS, verify the workload, and measure downtime and data-transfer time. Decide whether `tf` should refuse or warn when a placement change would strand a volume. Use the commented second Colima VM already present in inventory.nix (colima-b) so the move can be tested across hosts locally.
acceptance_criteria: A runbook covers data movement (snapshot/restore or restic), placement and DNS cutover, verification and rollback. A cross-host move is rehearsed in dev using the two Colima hosts (the commented colima-b in inventory.nix:76-77 is already there; use/uncomment it and set placement) and timed, including a stateful guest. A low-risk stateful move is dry-run in the homelab or explicitly deferred with a recorded reason. Downtime, data path and failure modes are recorded. 'task up' behavior on a data-bearing placement move is documented or guarded. Linked to xp2, sl8, 6zs and 93o.

title: Recover and contain the operator control plane (Mac)
description: 182 covers the age key and 1hg covers OpenTofu state, but the Mac is also the only working control plane: WireGuard client config, Incus remotes and client certificates, nix.linux-builder, the Colima dev profile, SSH keys, and the repo checkout. Losing it or having it stolen blocks fleet management even after secrets and state are recovered. The dev CA clone can also mint production-trusted certificates. Inventory what exists only on the Mac; write and rehearse a rebuild runbook on a clean or second machine that reaches task plan and task deploy; write a compromise response (rotate the age key and rekey sops, revoke Incus client certs, WireGuard and SSH keys, rotate the dev CA/intermediate and confirm no production-trusted leaf remains); link the break-glass path from 182.
acceptance_criteria: Mac-only inventory checked in; clean-machine rehearsal completes plan and deploy for one workload; compromise checklist rehearsed at least as a tabletop; recovery time recorded; 182 and 1hg cross-linked.
notes: Low likelihood, high impact. Distinct from 182 (secret loss) and 1hg (state): this is the ability to operate the fleet.

title: Define the nixpkgs and base-image upgrade cadence
description: flake.lock is updated by hand and images:nixos/26.05 is repeated in every terraform/<name>/default.nix (12 copies). Apart from nix-workloads-v6m (removing the HA band-aid), there is no plan for taking nixpkgs or the base image forward. Define a cadence: update the flake, deploy and verify in dev, roll out to the homelab with snapshots and a rollback step, and bump the base image when NixOS 26.11 ships. Centralize the image string in inventory.nix/modules so a bump is one edit.
acceptance_criteria: The image is a single inventory/module value used by every terraform config; a written cadence covers nix flake update, dev validation, homelab rollout and rollback; one full cycle is executed and recorded (including what broke and how it was rolled back).
notes: Coordination: host OS and Incus daemon upgrades live in nix-homelab-hosts; keep the two cadences linked. The Postgres major-version path is nix-workloads-v2l.

title: Make the secrets and access root recoverable
description: All sops decryption roots at the Mac's ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 (SOPS_AGE_KEY_CMD in the devshell), and no offline recovery recipient exists: losing the Mac or that key means the secrets, the step-ca intermediate and the CA material can no longer be decrypted or rekeyed. Add a break-glass path: an offline/paper age recipient in every relevant .sops.yaml rule, a documented recovery procedure (including break-glass SSH access to the guests), and a CI check that each sopsFile's recipients match exactly its consumers (no lockout, no over-sharing).
acceptance_criteria: An offline recovery age key is a recipient for every secret that must survive loss of the Mac; the recovery procedure is written and rehearsed by decrypting a secret with it; a check fails when a secret's recipients are missing a consumer or include an unintended one; break-glass access to a guest is documented and tested.

title: Move OpenTofu state off the Mac
description: The tf wrapper (flake.nix) runs tofu inside terraform/<name>/ with no backend block, and *.tfstate is gitignored. All instance, volume, profile and DNS state exists only on the Mac; losing it means every resource must be re-imported before the repo can manage the fleet again. Add a remote backend with locking (the backup volume, or the planned Garage/S3 from nix-workloads-6zs), migrate each workload's state, and document and automate recovery. Include a periodic state backup so a bad apply or a lost backend can be recovered.
acceptance_criteria: A backend with locking is configured in terraform/common.nix for every workload and the dns config; existing state is migrated without recreating resources; a second machine can run task plan against the same state; recovery from a lost backend is documented and rehearsed.
notes: Backend choice is open, not blocked: either the backup volume (proceed now) or Garage/S3 (nix-workloads-6zs). It is intentionally relates-only; if Garage is chosen, coordinate rather than wait.

title: Harden MQTT: persistence, per-user ACLs, availability
description: Enable broker persistence (message/session state on a volume so a restart or restore keeps retained state), replace the blanket 'pattern readwrite #' with per-user topic ACLs (z2m, hass, nr, exporter, p1ib), add birth/will availability for HA and z2m, set persistent_client_expiration and queue limits, and expose client/queued metrics. TLS is handled by the separate epic.
acceptance_criteria: Persistence enabled on a volume and included in local.backup.paths, with a restore-test assertion for retained/session state; per-user topic ACLs for z2m, hass, nr, exporter and p1ib replace readwrite #; birth/will availability for HA and z2m; persistent_client_expiration and queue limits set; client/queued metrics exposed; existing clients verified after a restart and a restore. TLS stays in dkp.3.
notes: Fold-in: once persistence lands, add the persistence path (expected /var/lib/mosquitto) to local.backup.paths and extend task restore-test to assert mosquitto state. restore-test currently omits mosquitto.

title: Local fallbacks for critical loads
description: Make the critical loads work with HA down: Zigbee direct binding for key lights/switches, the heating schedule held on the TRVs/thermostat, and an explicit list of automations that have no local fallback. Test by stopping HA for a while and walking the house. Document the fallback map (device -> what still works without HA).
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in fallback map (device/automation -> what still works without HA) covers the key lights, switches and heating. Zigbee direct binding is configured for the identified critical devices, and the heating schedule is held on the TRVs/thermostat rather than only in HA. There is an explicit list of automations with no local fallback, each with an accepted rationale. The behaviour is tested by stopping HA and walking the house, with results recorded. nix-workloads-c6z and nix-workloads-ka7 reference the map.

title: Rehearse MTTR: restore the smart-home stack onto the surviving Pi
description:
There is no spare Pi, so recovery means restoring the smart-home stack onto the surviving host. The two directions are not symmetric: the restic repositories and every Incus custom-volume snapshot live on rpi5-4gb, so losing rpi5-8gb is recoverable from the surviving rpi5-4gb, while losing rpi5-4gb loses the backup source and the snapshots (README "Known risks" and "Backups").

Write and time a runbook for the rpi5-8gb-loss case: move the Zigbee coordinator, recreate the instances, restore volumes from restic (snapshots are host-local and do not survive host loss), restore z2m state, start mosquitto -> z2m -> HA in order, repoint DNS, and verify lights/heating/MQTT. Record measured RTO/RPO and the gaps. The rpi5-4gb-loss case is gated on nix-workloads-o1m; once the offsite copy exists (or 6zs provides a replicated Garage backend and restic endpoints on both hosts), rehearse it the same way.

Depends on the basic drill (nix-workloads-5th). Close only after a timed dry run, then update nix-workloads-xp2 with the result.
acceptance_criteria: The runbook covers both host-loss directions and states the asymmetry explicitly: losing rpi5-8gb is restorable from the surviving rpi5-4gb restic repos; losing rpi5-4gb loses the restic server and its host-local volume snapshots, so that path is gated on nix-workloads-o1m (or a replicated Garage/restic backend) and is either rehearsed there or recorded as an accepted gap. Volume snapshots are never presented as usable after host loss. The rpi5-8gb-loss dry run is timed end to end (coordinator move, recreate, restore, start order, DNS, verify lights/heating/MQTT) with measured RTO/RPO, commands, failures and gaps. nix-workloads-xp2 is updated with the result.

title: Basic backup + restore drill (learn the flow)
description:
Learn and prove the backup/restore flow end to end, simply: pick one backed-up guest, run the daily restic path, restore a snapshot into a scratch path (or ENV=dev), verify the data (HA config + recorder dump, z2m state, node-red flows), and write the exact commands and gotchas into README 'Restore drill'.

Tooling already exists: `task restore-test`, `ENV=dev task dr-restore`, `task dr-restore-all` and the README section. The remaining work is an executed homelab run with results and gotchas recorded (plus a dev rehearsal), not building the flow. Start local-only; the offsite work (nix-workloads-o1m) extends this same drill rather than inventing another.
acceptance_criteria: The drill is executed end to end against homelab backups (and rehearsed in dev), not just documented as tooling. It covers restic check, restoring a snapshot to a scratch path, and content assertions for HA (config and recorder dump), Node-RED flows, z2m state, Kanidm and step-ca. The exact commands, timing and gotchas are recorded in README 'Restore drill'. Any gaps found are filed as beads. The offsite extension is left to nix-workloads-o1m.
notes: Tooling already landed: task restore-test, ENV=dev task dr-restore and the README 'Restore drill' section exist. Remaining work is an executed run with results/gotchas recorded (and a homelab pass), not building the flow.

title: TLS + mTLS for MQTT
description: Move mosquitto from plain 1883 to 8883 with server TLS (step-ca) and mTLS client certs for z2m/hass/nr/exporter; handle p1ib and any constrained devices per the compatibility matrix. Disable 1883 or bind it to loopback only. Keep the per-user ACLs and availability topics working. Done when no cleartext MQTT crosses the bridge or LAN and every client reconnects verified.
acceptance_criteria: Mosquitto serves MQTT over 8883 with a step-ca server certificate and mTLS for every capable client (z2m, HA, node-red, exporter); p1ib/ESP follow dkp.1's matrix or a recorded exception. Cleartext 1883 is disabled or bound to loopback only. Per-user ACLs, birth/will availability and persistence from 4eg still work. No cleartext MQTT crosses the bridge or LAN. Every client reconnects verified after a broker restart, and a restore of the broker state still works.

title: Client certificate lifecycle: issue, rotate, revoke, alert
description: Make mTLS client certs operationally boring: choose step-ca X.509 provisioners vs ACME, decide where keys live (sops/age per guest), automate renewal on NixOS, support revocation, and alert on expiry. Cover the onboarding path so a new guest gets its cert automatically, and document an emergency revoke. Enforce server-side verification of client certs for every service that accepts mTLS. Blocks the metrics and restic TLS work.
acceptance_criteria: A provisioner model is chosen and recorded. Client certificates are issued and renewed automatically on NixOS for every mTLS consumer, with keys stored per guest in sops/age and never in the Nix store. Revocation works and is tested; an emergency revoke procedure is documented. Expiry is alerted before it can break a link. Adding a new guest gets it a certificate through a documented, automated onboarding path. Every server that accepts mTLS actually verifies the client certificate against the CA. At least one issue/rotate/revoke cycle is rehearsed in dev, and 8xp and s9w are cross-linked.

title: TLS/mTLS compatibility matrix for MQTT clients (p1ib/ESP)
description: Determine TLS/mTLS capability per MQTT client: zigbee2mqtt/HA/node-red (NixOS - full CA + client cert), mosquitto-exporter (Go), and p1ib plus any ESP/firmware devices (can they validate a private CA? present client certs? memory headroom?). Method: check firmware/docs and test against a staging 8883 listener using step-ca certs. Output: a per-client matrix (mTLS / TLS-only / impossible) that decides the MQTT TLS rollout and records any documented exceptions. Blocks MQTT TLS+mTLS.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in matrix lists every MQTT client (zigbee2mqtt, HA, node-red, mosquitto-exporter, p1ib and any ESP/firmware device) with: mTLS / TLS-only / impossible verdict, whether it can validate a private CA, whether it can present a client cert, memory/battery headroom, and the source of evidence (firmware docs or a staging test). The verdicts are proven against a staging 8883 listener with step-ca certs where the client allows it. Every TLS-only or impossible client gets a documented compensating control (ACL + network policy). The matrix decides the rollout and is linked from dkp and dkp.3.

title: TLS/mTLS everywhere across workload links
description:
Every workload-to-workload link should be TLS at minimum and mTLS where the client can present a certificate, verified against the Esselius root via step-ca. Scope: MQTT, the metrics path (Alloy remote_write + central scrapes), restic REST, and an audit of the remaining intra-guest HTTP links (node-red->HA, Grafana->VM/Loki, homepage, nginx->loopback backends) with documented exceptions.

Requirements: no insecure_skip_verify anywhere; cert issuance/rotation/revocation automated; expiry alerted; a per-link matrix (link -> protocol -> auth -> gap) checked into the repo (README or docs/). Constrained devices (p1ib, ESP sensors) may not validate a private CA or present client certs - TLS+ACL+network policy is the recorded fallback per client.

Children: MQTT TLS+mTLS, metrics path, restic transport, constrained-client matrix, client-cert lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: Every in-scope link is TLS at minimum and mTLS where the client can present a certificate, verified against the Esselius root via step-ca, with no insecure_skip_verify anywhere. A per-link matrix (link -> protocol -> auth -> gap) is checked in and every exception is documented with an owner and rationale (HomeKit/HAP and constrained p1ib/ESP clients are explicit exceptions, not silent gaps). MQTT (dkp.3), the metrics path (dkp.4) and the restic transport (dkp.5) are migrated and verified; the constrained-client matrix (dkp.1) and client-cert lifecycle (dkp.2) are complete; CA root/intermediate custody and rotation are owned by s9w. No in-scope cleartext traffic remains on the bridge or LAN, and all clients reconnect verified.
notes: Out of scope here (owned by nix-homelab-hosts): Unbound DNS, WireGuard, and the Incus API (already client-cert authenticated). HomeKit/HAP keeps its own pairing protocol rather than CA TLS - record it as a documented exception, not a gap.

title: Pilot: reimplement one Node-RED flow as HA YAML in dev
description: Pick one representative existing Node-RED flow (for example a light or heating schedule with a condition) and reimplement it as an HA YAML/Nix automation in dev. Compare agent authoring, diff and review, config validation, deploy/rollback, and debugging against the Node-RED flow. Then force a realistic failure (wrong condition, missing trigger, stale state) and capture how you would explain and report it in each model: HA Trace/Logbook versus Node-RED debug/status. Record what was easy, what was hard, and whether HA YAML covers the common cases. Do not change homelab flows yet.
acceptance_criteria: One real flow runs in dev as HA YAML; config check passes; the change is diffable and reviewable; a failure walkthrough with trace/log artifacts and a note on which model gives the better bug-report experience; notes on authoring, testing, debugging and gaps versus Node-RED; a recommendation to nix-workloads-a7q.

title: Apply minimal config and retire experiment tuning
description:
Deploy the reduced workload config in dev, verify, then homelab; rebuild hosts; run doctor/verify/snapshots; watch OOM, PSI and NVMe swap for 24-48h. Remove dead experiment scaffolding (density KSM panels and stale baseline text) and reconcile the experiment beads: close E1-E4, confirm E5's already-recorded close (ybt) and leave E6 deferred/deferred-scoped.

Note: E5 (nix-workloads-ybt) is already closed and E6 (nix-workloads-6md) is deferred. Do not re-close them; state their disposition in EXPERIMENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: Dev and homelab verification pass; 48h clean (no OOM, no PSI rise, no disk-swap growth); config is smaller than before; E1-E4 are closed, E5 (ybt) is confirmed as already closed, and E6 (6md) is left deferred with its disposition recorded; dashboards/docs reflect the steady state.

title: Return host memory/zram settings to simple defaults
description: In nix-homelab-hosts, prefer upstream/NixOS defaults over experiment-era zram/swappiness/page-cluster/PSI tweaks for the mostly-idle 8GB/4GB pair. Remove KSM and any density experiment knobs; keep PSI only if it is still useful. Document why any remaining non-default exists and how to roll back.
acceptance_criteria: Host memory/zram config is at least as simple as stock; any remaining non-default is justified; hosts rebuilt; task doctor/verify pass; no disk-swap or NVMe regression.

title: Delete unnecessary workload overrides; keep only measured exceptions
description: Start from the shared container profile and remove per-guest memory/swap/OOM overrides that the baseline does not justify. Keep an override only for a measured spike or to protect HA/MQTT/zigbee2mqtt. Prefer deleting over adjusting. Reconcile E1/E2/E3/E5; update inventory comments/README if the policy changes. Dev deploy+verify first, then homelab.
acceptance_criteria: Each remaining override has a one-line reason; the diff is mostly deletions; dev verify passes; rollout plan recorded; experiment beads reconciled.

title: Measure only enough to justify deletions (7/30 days)
description: Find what actually needs an override, not a tuning matrix. Over 7 and 30 days, pull per-guest p95/p99 memory current/anon/file, OOM and swap-cap events, PSI and refaults, plus host MemAvailable, zram and NVMe writes. Flag only outliers and the critical services that need protection; everything else is a candidate for deleting its override.
acceptance_criteria: A short list of guests with a measured need plus host headroom, with queries/window; an explicit list of overrides that can be removed; no fine-grained per-guest tuning proposals.
notes: Window: 7-day data is enough to unblock .2/.3 (~2026-10-25); the 30-day pass (to ~2026-11-17) is confirmation, not a gate. Do not stall the epic waiting for 30 days.

title: Minimize resource tuning for a mostly idle homelab
description: The fleet is mostly idle and the current limits, swap caps, OOM priorities and zram settings are leftovers from the density experiments (E1-E7). Bias toward tuning as little as possible: delete experiment-era overrides, return to upstream/NixOS defaults where safe, and keep only overrides that a measurement or a concrete protection need justifies. The target is a smaller, simpler config - not a finely tuned one. If a workload is fine on the shared profile and the host has headroom, remove its override. Dev-first, then homelab.
acceptance_criteria: Fewer overrides than today; every remaining limit/swap/OOM/host knob has a recorded reason (measured need or critical-service protection); defaults are documented; dev deploy+verify and homelab doctor/verify pass; no OOM, PSI rise or disk-swap growth; E1-E5 reconciled.

title: Choose an agent-maintainable automation model
description: Agents now do most of the automation work; Node-RED was chosen for a human editing flows in a UI. Decide the authoring/runtime model for the next phase, keeping the runtime deterministic for lights and heating while agents author, review, test and deploy. Explainability is a first-class requirement: a human must be able to see how an automation works, why it did or did not fire, and produce a bug report with a trace or visual artifact. Options: HA YAML/Nix automations (best text, diff and test ergonomics; native automation traces and logbook), AppDaemon/Python (complex logic, logs but no native trace), Node-RED flows-as-code (visual canvas and live debug, but JSON is noisy for agents), n8n/Windmill (UI plus code and execution history, but heavier), and agent-at-runtime (ad-hoc only). Recommendation: pilot HA YAML for the common cases, keep Node-RED only for flows that need visual debugging, then decide migrate versus split. The pilot is nix-workloads-i5v.
acceptance_criteria: A model is chosen and recorded after the pilot: where each class of automation lives (HA YAML, Node-RED, code), how agents author, review, test and deploy it, how credentials and rollback work, and whether Node-RED is retained, shrunk or retired. The chosen model has a documented explainability path: readable definition, per-run trace or execution history, and a visual indicator or dashboard sufficient to file a bug report. The runtime for lights and heating remains deterministic. If Node-RED is retained, the decision includes a flows versioning/export path (git-backed or generated) and how agents diff and review flows.
notes: Node-RED has projects/git plugins; evaluate them if NR survives the decision. Flows currently live only in /var/lib/node-red and backups.

title: Migrate Home Assistant automations to YAML packages in the repo
description: HA is UI-configured (.storage), so agents can read but not diff or review automations. Move automations/scripts to services.home-assistant.config packages, add config check to verify, and keep the .storage migration path in README.

title: Power and WAN resilience for the closet
description:
North-star goal: the closet survives power cuts and WAN outages gracefully.

Scope: UPS/battery for both Pis and the router, graceful shutdown and auto-restart, 4G/5G or secondary WAN failover, local NTP/DNS, and measured ride-through. Requires hardware, so scope a minimum viable version first (one UPS, one cellular modem) before expanding.

Extends the accepted power/router risks in nix-workloads-c6z and the time work in nix-workloads-5u0, and complements nix-workloads-xp2 (host maintenance) and nix-workloads-ozj (thermal).
acceptance_criteria: A UPS/battery protects the Pis and network gear long enough for graceful shutdown, with auto-restart verified. A WAN failover path (cellular or secondary link) is configured and measured. Hosts and guests shut down and come back cleanly, and the home critical path is verified after each event. Ride-through and failover times are recorded. Monitoring alerts on power/WAN state.

title: Zero standing secrets and workload identity
description:
North-star goal: no shared static passwords for workload links.

Every guest gets a short-lived identity or certificate from step-ca; service-to-service auth is mTLS or short-lived tokens; the network is default-deny; rotation needs no downtime; compromise of one guest does not expose another.

The nix-workloads-dkp epic is the first tranche (TLS/mTLS across MQTT, metrics and restic) and nix-workloads-dso is the repository-auth tranche. This epic is the end state: workload identity, default-deny, containment and a complete exception-aware link matrix (HomeKit/HAP and constrained ESP devices are documented exceptions).

Extends nix-workloads-dkp, nix-workloads-dso, nix-workloads-8xp, nix-workloads-485, nix-workloads-rgc and nix-workloads-s9w.
acceptance_criteria: Every in-scope guest-to-guest link uses a short-lived identity (mTLS or short-lived token), with no shared static password. Default-deny network policy is in place. Credentials and certificates rotate without downtime and are alerted before expiry. A compromise test shows one guest cannot read or control another workload's data or broker topics. Exceptions are documented. The link matrix is complete and checked in.

title: Smart-home infrastructure as code with progressive delivery
description:
North-star goal: every change to the smart home is a reviewed, tested, reversible deploy.

Automations, dashboards, helpers, areas, integrations, MQTT ACLs and credentials should be versioned; CI should validate them; an ephemeral dev twin should run the change; rollout should be health-gated and auto-roll back on regression.

Extends nix-workloads-a7q (authoring model), nix-workloads-i5v (pilot), nix-workloads-0t1 (HA UI state), nix-workloads-udk (VM tests) and nix-workloads-kvm (drift). Builds on the closed nix-workloads-ku8 (HA automations in YAML).
acceptance_criteria: Automations, dashboards, helpers and integrations are versioned or reproducibly exported, with a documented UI-only remainder. CI validates config and runs the dev twin. One real change goes through health-gated rollout with automatic rollback on a failing check. Drift detection runs on a schedule. The pipeline and its limits are documented in README.

title: Offline-first house: the home works through a long internet outage
description:
North-star goal: the house keeps working for an extended internet outage.

Lights, heating, Zigbee and local admin must not depend on WAN, public DNS, Kanidm, Home Assistant or any cloud service. Scope: ESP/p1ib local behavior, TRV/thermostat schedules, local DNS and NTP, break-glass identity, and a documented list of accepted cloud dependencies.

Start with nix-workloads-env (local fallbacks) and nix-workloads-6sk (identity break-glass), then run a real internet-off day. Target a week once the fallbacks are proven. This is the most user-visible ambition in the repo.
acceptance_criteria: An internet-off drill of at least 24h (target one week) keeps lights, heating, Zigbee and local admin working. The fallback map is checked in and tested. Every remaining cloud/WAN dependency in the critical path is documented with a fallback or an accepted reason. Local DNS and time survive WAN loss. Findings update nix-workloads-env, nix-workloads-6sk and nix-workloads-93o.

title: Automated single-host survivability (not HA)
description:
North-star goal: if either Pi dies, the critical path is rehydrated on the survivor with minimal human intervention.

This is guided or automated recovery, not a two-node HA cluster: there is no quorum, the hosts share power/router failure domains, and the Zigbee coordinator is a physical SPOF. The system should detect host loss, move or recreate guests, flip DNS, use replicated Garage or an off-pair copy for state, enforce start order (mosquitto -> zigbee2mqtt -> Home Assistant), and verify lights/heating/MQTT.

Start with the human-gated runbook from nix-workloads-sl8, then automate the safe steps. Extends nix-workloads-xp2, nix-workloads-93o, nix-workloads-6zs and nix-workloads-4xa.
acceptance_criteria: A simulated loss of either host triggers a documented rehydration of the critical path on the survivor (human-gated first, automated where safe). The flow handles placement, DNS, state source, start order and verification, and records measured recovery time. It does not assume quorum or shared storage. At least one direction is demonstrated in dev or homelab; the other is gated on the off-pair/replicated state path. The runbook and automation are linked from nix-workloads-xp2 and nix-workloads-sl8.

title: Add storage integrity cadence: btrfs scrub and SMART self-tests
description: The btrfs and nodes dashboards monitor checksum errors, I/O errors and wear after the fact, and ozj covers thermal, throttle and wear, but nothing schedules a btrfs scrub or SMART self-tests. Add scrub and short/long SMART self-test timers on both hosts, alerts for failures and pending sectors, and a runbook for a failing device (restore from backup, replace, rebuild). There is no RAID, so a scrub detects but cannot repair; the value is early warning and exercising the restore path.
acceptance_criteria: btrfs scrub and SMART self-tests are scheduled on both hosts (in nix-homelab-hosts or documented there). Failures and pending sectors route to ntfy. A runbook covers a failing device, including backup restore and replacement. The checks are visible in monitoring and task doctor or verify. Linked to ozj, 13n and 3kb.

title: Bring Home Assistant UI state (dashboards, helpers, integrations) under code or drift checks
description: a7q, i5v and the closed ku8 cover automations, but dashboards, helpers, areas, integrations and the MQTT client credentials used by Home Assistant and Node-RED live in application state (`.storage`). They are backed up but not diffable, reviewable or reproducible. Decide what must be code-managed versus UI-managed, move dashboards/helpers (at least) into the repo or add a reproducible export/sync tool, add a drift check, and document the UI-only remainder. Cover the rotation path for credentials that live only in `.storage`, since 8xp rotates MQTT/OIDC credentials and the broker secret is not the same copy Home Assistant uses.
acceptance_criteria: An explicit split of code-managed versus UI-managed Home Assistant state is documented. Dashboards and helpers are in the repo or exported by a reproducible tool. A drift check runs in verify or CI. MQTT and OIDC client credentials have a documented rotation path that updates application state. README is updated and a7q, i5v, udk and 8xp are cross-linked.

title: Baseline guest and host hardening plus access lifecycle
description: nix-workloads-485 audits exposure, nix-workloads-8xp rotates credentials, nix-workloads-rp6 recovers the Mac and nix-workloads-182 recovers secrets, but there is no baseline hardening or access lifecycle. Cover SSH/user/sudo policy, the host no-AppArmor trade-off and the lxc credential shim, WireGuard peer add/remove/rotation, OIDC client and human onboarding/offboarding, Incus client certificates, and the credentials that live outside sops (Cachix auth, router admin, GitHub, SSH keys, and the Mac-side Attic client token). The Attic *server* token is sops-managed in secrets/attic.yaml - do not list it as outside sops. Add a cheap drift check and a join/leave procedure. Include an explicit decision on whether software TPM devices are adopted (see the separate analysis; initial recommendation is no for the current container fleet).
acceptance_criteria: A baseline hardening document covers SSH, users, firewall and the no-AppArmor trade-off. An access matrix covers humans, agents, WireGuard, OIDC clients and Incus certificates. Join and leave procedures are tested. Every non-sops credential is inventoried with an owner and a recovery/rotation path, and sops-held credentials are distinguished from Mac-only ones (the Attic server token is in secrets/attic.yaml; only the Mac client token is outside). A cheap check detects drift. The TPM decision is recorded with rationale. Linked to 485, 8xp, rp6, 182 and j4l.

title: Define the host/workload compatibility contract and rehearse a bare-metal rebuild
description: The workloads repo assumes host-provided building blocks: `incusbr-vpn`, the host Unbound resolver, CA/cache trust, client certificates, the persistent pool and the platform CA. Those live in nix-homelab-hosts, and a host change or rebuild can break every guest with no check. Write the contract down (required host settings/versions and the interfaces this repo consumes), add a cheap compatibility check (evaluate/plan, or a script that asserts the required host state), and rehearse a bare-metal rebuild from nix-homelab-hosts through `task plan`, `task deploy` and `task verify`.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in contract lists every host-provided dependency (bridge, DNS resolver, pool, CA trust, cache endpoint/key, client cert, platform CA) with the owning file in nix-homelab-hosts. A script or check fails when a required host interface is missing or differs. A bare-metal rebuild of one host is rehearsed from empty media (or the closest dev equivalent) through plan/deploy/verify, timed, with gaps filed. Linked from README and from 4k8, m2x and xp2.

title: Schedule fleet verification and configuration drift detection
description: task verify and task plan only run by hand, so silent drift (failed unit, wrong closure, DNS record, resource change) stays invisible. Add a scheduled run (timer or CI) that verifies every guest in an env and reports failures through ntfy. Once 1hg lands, add tofu plan -detailed-exitcode per workload and for dns against the remote backend, plus a live-vs-inventory DNS comparison. Start with verify, which works today, and add plan when state is remote; make failures actionable and link to the incident playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduled verify covers every guest and reports drift; plan-based drift check runs for workloads and dns after 1hg; failures reach ntfy with the workload and reason; README documents scope and cadence; 1hg and xp2 cross-linked.
notes: Two phases: verify can start now; plan-based drift waits on 1hg.

title: Test the Home Assistant Postgres major-version upgrade path
description: 4k8 covers nixpkgs and base-image cadence and lsf covers retention, but nothing covers a Postgres major bump under the Home Assistant recorder. On dev, restore a production HA dump, perform the upgrade (prefer pg_upgrade, fall back to dump and restore), verify HA loads and history queries work, measure downtime and disk headroom, and document rollback using a snapshot plus dump. Fold the step into the 4k8 cadence and the restore drill.
acceptance_criteria: Dev rehearsal from a real production dump succeeds; downtime and disk headroom measured; rollback verified; procedure checked in; 4k8, 5th and lsf cross-linked.

title: Define and rehearse credential rotation
description:
nix-workloads-182 recovers secrets, nix-workloads-dkp.2 handles client certificates, and nix-workloads-s9w owns the CA hierarchy (root and intermediate custody, expiry and rotation). This bead covers everything else; do not duplicate CA rotation here.

Define a cadence and owner, a procedure that updates sops and every consumer without downtime, and a revocation path for at least:
- MQTT users and passwords (z2m, hass, nr, exporter, p1ib), Postgres roles, restic REST creds and the restic repository password/rekey, Grafana admin password and secret key, ntfy topic, OIDC client secrets (grafana, node-red, homepage, oauth2-proxy), node-red credential secret, homepage cookie secret, Kanidm idm admin password, Home Assistant long-lived token, Attic token, and the Zigbee2MQTT network key (or an explicit exclusion, since rotating it means re-pairing devices).

Derive the matrix from secrets/*.yaml and .sops.yaml rather than trusting this list; record any credential that lives outside sops (Mac client tokens, router admin, GitHub, SSH). Rehearse one credential end to end in dev and record timing and rollback. Link the CA-owned items to nix-workloads-s9w.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in rotation matrix covers every credential in secrets/ and outside it: secret -> owner -> cadence -> consumers -> procedure -> rollback, with explicit exclusions and reasons. The step-ca root/intermediate hierarchy is delegated to nix-workloads-s9w rather than duplicated. At least one end-to-end rotation is rehearsed in dev without service interruption (for example an MQTT user password), with timing recorded. A revocation/emergency path and a restic-repository rekey path are documented. nix-workloads-182, nix-workloads-dkp.2 and nix-workloads-s9w are cross-linked and the runbook is linked from README.

title: Audit inbound exposure and authorization of every workload
description: dkp covers encryption, but no bead asserts who can reach what. Build a checked-in exposure and authorization matrix: listener -> interface (LAN macvlan, WireGuard, incus bridge), intended clients, auth mechanism (Kanidm OIDC, Home Assistant local account, Incus client cert, Attic token, none), and firewall rule. Confirm every admin or UI endpoint requires auth and the right group (Home Assistant, Node-RED, Grafana, Homepage, z2m, Attic, Incus), that constrained devices get only broker access, and that guest egress is intentional. Record exceptions such as HomeKit and p1ib/ESP instead of leaving them implicit, and add a cheap check where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Exposure and authorization matrix checked in; every listener justified; no unintended unauthenticated admin endpoint; exceptions documented with owners; dkp.3 and 182 cross-linked; required firewall or ACL changes filed or made.

title: Make guest DNS resolution survive loss of the default host
description: modules/local.nix gives every guest the default host resolver address (dnsAddress from envs.<env>.defaultHost), so backup and homepage on rpi5-4gb resolve through rpi5-8gb at 10.6.0.3. If rpi5-8gb dies, those guests lose name resolution and therefore TLS, MQTT and backup reconnects. Wire guests to their own host resolver or to a redundant pair, update the inventory comment, and test with the default resolver unavailable. xp2 promises DNS stays available; make the mechanism explicit.
acceptance_criteria: Guests resolve through their host resolver or a redundant resolver; test with the default-host resolver blocked or stopped passes; DNS dashboard and client resolution still work; inventory comment updated; sl8 and xp2 reference the mechanism.

title: Write incident playbooks for the critical path
description: sl8 covers total host loss, but there are no per-service playbooks. Add short, testable playbooks for mosquitto down or refusing clients, Home Assistant down, zigbee2mqtt bridge offline, Node-RED or the automation runtime down, DNS failure, expired certificate, disk full, backup target unavailable, and monitoring unavailable. Each should list symptoms, first checks, safe mitigation, rollback, verification, and what to record. Walk through at least one in dev and link the playbooks from README.
acceptance_criteria: Playbooks checked in for each listed failure; at least one walked through in dev with commands verified; linked from README and the local-fallback documentation; sl8, xp2 and 122 cross-linked.

title: Document Zigbee coordinator failure and replacement
description: Zigbee2MQTT backs up the coordinator data and the network key is in sops, but there is no runbook for a dead dongle. Write a short procedure: identify the coordinator by /dev/serial/by-id, keep the same IEEE address and network key, restore the z2m database and coordinator backup, verify devices, and list what needs re-pairing if the identity cannot be preserved. Include a spare-hardware recommendation and expected recovery time, and link it from README Known risks.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook checked in; covers both preserve-identity and worst-case re-pair paths; states what the z2m backup does and does not contain; spare recommendation recorded; linked from Known risks and xkz.
notes: User asked for minor documentation, not a full rehearsal.

title: Review thermal, throttle and wear monitoring for the 28C closet
description: Host wear and temperature metrics already exist, but both Pis live in a warm closet at about 28C ambient, so thermal headroom and throttling need an explicit review. Audit current coverage and thresholds for SoC temperature, throttle and undervoltage flags, NVMe/SD SMART wear and lifetime writes, and fan/thermal state. Add missing collectors, alerts and panels with thresholds tied to the enclosure and ambient, and record the expected seasonal headroom. Power-loss/UPS safety remains a separate question.
acceptance_criteria: Coverage matrix checked in (metric -> source -> alert threshold); missing collectors and alerts added; a synthetic or hot-day throttle test alerts correctly; dashboard shows temperature, throttle and wear per host; README documents the 28C constraint and expected limits.
notes: xp2 covers planned reboots, not degradation. Monitoring already has NVMe write and btrfs panels.

title: Upstream the LXC credential generator shim
description: modules/lxc-credentials.nix overlays distrobuilder's generator to stop it clearing LoadCredential for non-nested containers. AGENTS.md documents this as belonging upstream (nixpkgs #260670, distrobuilder #985) and notes upstream reverted an earlier attempt. Research the current upstream state, propose the narrow fix (drop only LoadCredential, leave ImportCredential cleared), and remove the local overlay once it lands. Research-heavy: check PR/issue status and the AppArmor assumptions first.
acceptance_criteria: The upstream issue/PR status is summarized; a minimal patch or upstream contribution is proposed or filed; if accepted, the local overlay and its per-guest opt-in are removed and the fleet verified with 0 failed units.

title: Rehearse provision-all from an empty host
description: nix-workloads-sl8 covers restoring onto the surviving Pi by hand. Nothing verifies that the repo can build the fleet from zero: DNS, onboarding, cache bootstrap, first deploy (COPY=1) and restore. Automate a fresh-environment rehearsal in dev: destroy the VM/guests, run provision-all, restore state, and verify the stack. This catches ordering bugs (DNS before guests, attic/step-ca bootstrap, sops recipients) that only appear on a clean run.
acceptance_criteria: A task destroys and rebuilds the dev env from scratch via provision-all (including DNS and cache bootstrap) without manual steps; state is restored and the stack verified; the full run is timed and any gaps are filed or fixed. The same flow is documented as the bare-metal rebuild path.

title: Automatically verify backups are actually restorable
description: task restore-test and ENV=dev task dr-restore prove restorability, but only when someone runs them. Add a lightweight, non-destructive verification that runs on a schedule and alerts on failure: restic check --read-data-subset against each guest repo plus an automated restore of a sample snapshot into a scratch path (preferably in dev) with basic content assertions. Keep it far cheaper than a full drill; this is a canary, not the MTTR rehearsal.
acceptance_criteria: A scheduled job verifies every backed-up guest's repo can be read and a sample snapshot restores; failure routes to ntfy with the guest and reason; the check is visible in the Backups dashboard; README documents what it does and does not prove.

title: Add NixOS VM tests for the critical guests
description: Only example has a VM test (packages.aarch64-linux.example-vm); nix flake check otherwise evaluates configurations without booting them. Add VM tests for the smart-home path: mosquitto (sops/credentials, per-user ACLs, persistence across restart), the restic backup module (backup then restore a file), and Home Assistant (config loads, custom components build). Run them in CI on the aarch64 runner where possible and document the KVM/local path.
acceptance_criteria: VM tests exist for mosquitto, backup/restore and Home Assistant; they boot the service and assert the critical behaviour, not just evaluation; they are wired into a task and (where the runner supports KVM) CI; the tests fail if the corresponding service or secret wiring breaks.

title: Smart-home inventory: floorplan, rooms, models, batteries
description: Build a checked-in smart-home inventory: a floorplan (image/SVG or Mermaid) plus a per-room device list with vendor/model, protocol, power source, and battery cell type + count. Bootstrap from Zigbee2MQTT bridge/devices and the HA area/device registry, then annotate rooms/floorplan manually. Deliver a stock list (e.g. keep N x CR2032, 2 x AA) and optionally a script that diffs live Z2M devices against the doc. No secrets or network keys in the document.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in inventory has a floorplan (image/SVG or Mermaid) and a per-room device list with vendor/model, protocol, power source, and battery cell type + count. It is bootstrapped from the Zigbee2MQTT bridge/devices and the HA area/device registry, then annotated per room. It produces a stock list (for example N x CR2032, 2 x AA). An optional script diffs live Z2M devices against the document. The document contains no secrets, network keys or credentials.

title: Zigbee RF + coordinator hygiene
description: Experiment: put the coordinator on a USB extension away from the Pi/USB3, choose a channel that does not overlap the 2.4 GHz WiFi plan, add router devices for weak links, and baseline linkquality/LQI plus dropped messages before/after. Record method and measurements in EXPERIMENTS.md, not README.
acceptance_criteria: The coordinator is on a USB extension away from the Pi/USB3, on a Zigbee channel that does not overlap the 2.4 GHz WiFi plan, with router devices added for the weak links. Linkquality/LQI and dropped-message baselines are recorded before and after in EXPERIMENTS.md, with method and dates. The experiment has an explicit keep/revert conclusion, and xkz links the result to 629 and 3iq. No conclusions are written into README.

title: Smart-home alert coverage
description: Extend provision.alerting.rules beyond down/stale: entities unavailable or not updated in N, low battery per device, recorder DB growth/connections, MQTT client/queue anomalies, coordinator or z2m bridge offline, and HA backup age. Route to ntfy; group by device/room to avoid alert storms.
acceptance_criteria: Alert rules cover entities unavailable or not updated in N, low battery per device, recorder DB growth/connections, MQTT client/queue anomalies, coordinator/z2m bridge offline, and HA backup age, in addition to the existing down/stale rules. Thresholds and routing to ntfy are recorded, alerts are grouped by device/room to avoid storms, and each class is exercised with a synthetic/test alert. No duplicate alerts are added where nix-workloads-13n or nix-workloads-lsf already owns them.

title: Home Assistant recorder retention + Postgres maintenance
description:
Set explicit recorder purge_keep_days, auto_purge and commit_interval; size the Postgres volume; verify autovacuum; add DB size/growth panels. Measure the current DB size first so the retention choice is informed rather than guessed.

Split of ownership with nix-workloads-13n: this bead owns retention, vacuum and the raw size/growth panels; 13n owns predict_linear days-to-full forecasting and its alerts. Do not add the same alert twice.
acceptance_criteria: Current Postgres size and growth are measured before choosing values. Explicit recorder purge_keep_days, auto_purge and commit_interval are set and survive a deploy; the volume is sized from the measured growth; autovacuum is verified. DB size/growth panels are added, while days-to-full forecasting and its alerts stay with nix-workloads-13n to avoid duplicate alerts. Retention and disk headroom are documented in README, and nix-workloads-122, nix-workloads-13n and nix-workloads-v2l are cross-linked.

title: TLS + mTLS for the restic backup transport
description: Serve the restic REST backend over HTTPS and authenticate with client certs (mTLS), instead of or alongside htpasswd. Update modules/backup.nix, the restic exporter, and secrets/backup.yaml. Prove it with a backup + restore, then retire the old basic-auth credentials.
design: Verify transport before committing: rest-server has TLS flags but may not require/verify client certificates. If it does not, terminate mTLS at the existing nginx/step-ca front end (or another proxy) and keep rest-server on loopback, rather than assuming native mTLS. If the restic backend moves to S3/Garage (nix-workloads-6zs), TLS/mTLS at the REST layer may be superseded by S3 HTTPS plus scoped credentials; record which model is used and do not build both.
acceptance_criteria: The restic transport is HTTPS with client authentication: mTLS (native rest-server support, or terminated at a documented proxy) or scoped S3 credentials if the backend moves to nix-workloads-6zs. No plaintext restic traffic remains on the LAN or bridge. A backup and a restore both succeed through the new transport, restore-test still passes, and the old basic-auth credential is retired or explicitly retained with a reason. The architecture (rest-server vs S3/Garage, where TLS terminates) is recorded in README and cross-linked from nix-workloads-dso and nix-workloads-6zs.

title: TLS + mTLS for the metrics path
description: Wrap Alloy remote_write and the central scrape of node/exporters in TLS+mTLS: server certs for VictoriaMetrics/Loki and scrape targets, client certs per guest, updated Alloy config and provisioning. No skip_verify; verify dashboards and alerts keep flowing after the switch.
acceptance_criteria: Alloy remote_write and the central scrape of node/exporters use TLS with client certificates issued by dkp.2, with no insecure_skip_verify. Server certificates cover the VictoriaMetrics/Loki and scrape endpoints, and provisioning is updated. After the switch the dashboards keep receiving data and the alert rules keep firing; a test alert is delivered. Rollback is documented and the per-link matrix is updated.

title: Run replicated S3 storage (Garage) on both hosts
description:
Run an S3-compatible object store as incus workloads on both rpi5-8gb and rpi5-4gb, replicated so the data survives either host failing. Primary uses to evaluate:
1. OpenTofu state backend (today it is gitignored local terraform.tfstate on the Mac).
2. The restic backup repositories: restic can talk S3 directly, potentially replacing the single rest-server on rpi5-4gb and giving every host a local endpoint. This interacts with nix-workloads-dso (per-guest auth) and nix-workloads-dkp.5 (transport), so record which model wins rather than building both.
3. Attic chunk storage: Attic supports S3, so moving it to Garage lets the build cache survive loss of rpi5-8gb (today Attic is a single workload on the default host).

Evaluate Garage (preferred for two-node replication), SeaweedFS and MinIO; decide engine, topology (Garage layout vs bucket replication), capacity/CPU/memory on the Pis, TLS via step-ca, and sops credentials. Resource cost matters: the pair is 8GB + 4GB and mostly idle, so measure before committing; if the cost is a large grab, keep the state backend only and leave restic/Attic alone. Note that replication across two nodes has quorum and split-brain trade-offs, and is not offsite - nix-workloads-o1m remains separate.

Solve the bootstrap chicken-and-egg: OpenTofu cannot create the store that holds its own state without a documented local/bootstrap state path and migration. Test in dev first.
acceptance_criteria: Engine and replication topology chosen and justified for two nodes, including the failure domain it does and does not cover (two nodes are not offsite; loss of both still loses the data). Both hosts serve the store in dev, with measured memory/CPU/disk cost on the 4GB Pi and a record of whether it fits alongside the existing guests. Each candidate use gets an explicit adoption decision: (a) OpenTofu state backend, (b) restic backing store in place of or behind rest-server, (c) Attic chunk storage. Every adopted use is tested; rejected uses are recorded with a reason. Adopting restic or Attic must not silently break nix-workloads-dso, nix-workloads-dkp.5 or the restore drill. OpenTofu backend is configured with state migrated and a documented bootstrap/restore path when one host is down; credentials via sops; restore drill covers it; offsite copy explicitly out of scope.
notes: Shared enabler (state backend for 1hg, relates to o1m/dkp.5/xp2) but nothing is hard-blocked on it; 1hg can ship on the backup volume instead. Promote to P1 only if Garage is chosen as the backend.

title: Make host maintenance and reboots safe for the home
description: Both rpi5-8gb and rpi5-4gb are standalone incus servers. Today a host reboot or upgrade can take internet/DNS, identity, MQTT/Zigbee and the lights/heating with it, even though most workloads could run on the other host. Define what must stay up and where it runs, then implement and rehearse a single-host maintenance path: move or duplicate critical services off the host being serviced, ensure guests auto-start, sequence reboots, and keep monitoring/alerting meaningful during the window. Accept an outage only where hardware pins a workload - notably the Zigbee USB dongle, which stays with its physical host. This is not full HA failover; it is safe, predictable maintenance.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, tested runbook for servicing either host, including the host with the Zigbee dongle: internet/DNS, MQTT/Zigbee (lights/heating) and identity stay available, or the unavoidable exception is explicitly listed. Guests auto-start after reboot; monitoring/alerts stay meaningful; verification and rollback steps are included; at least one maintenance window is rehearsed in dev and one in homelab.
notes:
Conclusion (2026-10): two standalone incus servers with no quorum (a 2-node cluster is a dolt anti-pattern) and no spare hardware; both Pis share power/router/WireGuard failure domains, and the coordinator is an irreducible SPOF. Decision: do not chase HA - minimize MTTR via a timed restore-onto-surviving-host runbook (nix-workloads-sl8) and local fallbacks (nix-workloads-env). Keep open until the timed dry run lands.
Now blocked on nix-workloads-sl8: the timed restore-onto-surviving-host dry run is the close condition, not a parallel nice-to-have.

title: Agent-operated fleet with guardrails
description:
North-star goal: agents can operate the fleet, not just edit files.

Agents should plan, test in dev, deploy, verify, roll back and file their own beads, under a policy that limits blast radius and keeps a human on the loop for critical changes. Includes a capability/policy model, audit trail, change classes, and a demonstrated end-to-end change.

Extends nix-workloads-a7q (authoring/runtime decision) and the dev-first rule, with nix-workloads-6da (doctor/static checks) and nix-workloads-kvm (drift) as safety rails. The ambition is the safety model, not the automation itself.
acceptance_criteria: An agent completes one workload change end to end: plan, dev deploy, verify, rollback drill and bead updates, under a documented policy. Change classes define what is autonomous vs human-gated. Every action is auditable (who/what/why, diff, verification result). Blast-radius limits and a kill switch are tested. The model is documented and adopted for at least one recurring task.

title: SLOs for the house, not just uptime
description:
North-star goal: measure what the household feels, not just whether a container is up.

Define SLOs for light command latency, heating schedule accuracy, dashboard freshness and backup age; add synthetic probes and error budgets; alert only on user-visible impact rather than every noisy metric.

Extends nix-workloads-122 (alert coverage), nix-workloads-ozj (thermal), nix-workloads-13n (capacity) and nix-workloads-3kb (backup canary). nix-workloads-ka7 should link the alerting model.
acceptance_criteria: Published SLOs exist for light command latency, heating schedule accuracy, dashboard freshness and backup age, with measurement method and targets. Synthetic probes exercise the user-visible path. Error budgets are tracked and alerts fire only when impact is real (or on burn rate). At least one month of data is available and reviewed.

title: Digital twin: test the house without touching the house
description:
North-star goal: test the house without touching the house.

Build a reproducible simulation environment with fake Zigbee devices, virtual TRVs/thermostats, MQTT replay and scripted failure injection, so automations, dashboards and recovery can be exercised in CI or on demand.

Extends nix-workloads-udk and nix-workloads-kvm, and uses the dev env. This needs a device simulator, not just NixOS VMs; the hard part is believable sensor/actuator behavior and replaying real traffic safely.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible simulation environment provides fake Zigbee/TRV devices and MQTT replay plus fault injection. At least three critical automations and one recovery scenario are tested end to end without physical devices. The environment is launched by a task and, where possible, wired into CI. Results and remaining gaps versus real hardware are documented.

title: Track custom Home Assistant component compatibility and upgrades
description: The repo maintains custom Home Assistant components under `pkgs/` (audi_connect_ha, easee_hass, pysignalr, passport-openidconnect). 4k8 covers nixpkgs and the base image, v6m covers the Home Assistant package band-aid, and udk may build them, but nothing tracks their upstream compatibility, pinned revision, security or owner. Add a manifest with upstream project, pinned version/revision, owner and test, include the components in the update cadence, and add a build or load test so a Home Assistant bump cannot silently break them.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest lists every custom component with upstream, pin, owner and test coverage. The update cadence includes them. A build or VM test loads them with Home Assistant. A broken upgrade has a documented rollback. Linked to 4k8, v6m and udk.

title: Decide and monitor time synchronization for the fleet
description: TLS, step-ca, ACME, logs and incident timelines all depend on correct time, but no bead owns the NTP source, fallback or drift alerting. Decide chrony versus timesyncd, internal versus public sources, and behavior when the internet is down. Apply the choice to hosts and guests as appropriate, monitor offset, and link the failure behavior into the outage model and incident playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: The time-source decision is recorded, including behavior without internet. Configuration is applied consistently to hosts and guests. Clock offset and sync failure are monitored and alert to ntfy. The outage model and ka7 reference the behavior. Linked to 4k8 and 93o.

title: Define workload decommissioning and orphan cleanup
description: Adding a workload is documented, but removing one is not. Define and automate the reverse: destroy the instance, delete or archive attached volumes and their snapshots, remove the inventory and DNS entry, remove the backup repository and restic exporter target, remove monitoring scrapes and dashboards, remove sops recipients, and clean the Terraform state and caches. Add an orphan check that finds leftover volumes, DNS records, monitoring targets or sops recipients.
acceptance_criteria: A checklist and a task or script remove a workload end to end. They are exercised on a disposable dev workload. An orphan check detects leftover volumes, DNS records, monitoring targets or unused sops recipients. README documents the procedure. No credentials, data or alerts are left behind.

title: Add disk-capacity forecasts and days-to-full alerts
description: Disk-space alerts fire at 15 percent free, but there is no forecast. Add predict_linear panels and alerts for host pools, guest volumes, the restic repository, Home Assistant Postgres, Loki and VictoriaMetrics, with days-to-full thresholds and per-host variables. Include backup growth against retention so a retention change is visible, document expected growth, and link the panels from the capacity dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Forecast panels and days-to-full alerts for host and guest volumes, restic, Postgres, Loki and VictoriaMetrics; alerts route to ntfy; thresholds documented; dashboards host-filterable; 3kb, lsf and 122 cross-linked.

title: Define Zigbee OTA firmware maintenance and scheduling
description: No policy exists for Zigbee device firmware. Evaluate Zigbee2MQTT OTA support (per-device ota settings, update and update_available topics, index override), then define an approach: inventory current firmware, an allowlist and maintenance window, one-device-at-a-time rollout with coordinator and z2m backup and rollback, and monitoring of failures and battery impact. Prefer an agent-owned recurring task that proposes updates and reports results; do not auto-update safety-critical devices without a rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: Z2M OTA capability documented for the device fleet; schedule, allowlist and maintenance window defined; one non-critical device updated and verified (or a documented reason not to); rollback path proven; recurring agent task or checklist specified; 87m and xkz cross-linked.
notes: ESP and p1ib firmware is separate; scope this bead to Zigbee OTA.
